episodeSummary: In this guest-free episode of FS Jam, Christopher and Anthony explore the surprisingly murky world of building third-party JavaScript widgets and SDKs, drawing on Christopher's experience creating Everfund's donation widget. They unpack why scripts must often be bundled to the aging UMD format rather than modern ESM (despite 93% browser support), the tradeoffs between private S3 hosting and npm CDNs, and the challenges of making one script work across React, Vue, WordPress, and plain HTML—including a baffling WordPress bug solved only by hosting the script inside the plugin itself. They weigh iframe-based rendering versus direct DOM injection, noting iframes avoid CORS issues and simplify updates but block CSS customization, and describe Everfund's move toward a headless donation SDK. The conversation then broadens to documentation philosophy via the Divio system (tutorials, how-tos, reference, explanation), plans for the Remix Conference in Utah, and the podcast's future: introducing sponsorships, possibly merchandise, balancing guest pitches with genuine education, and vetting products before endorsing them—Anthony even renounces Qovery on air. They close by reflecting on parasocial relationships with listeners and naming recent favorite episodes on Hydrogen, Flight Control, Kent C. Dodds, Orta, and Miško Hevery.
